test_title: PYST 1: SSC CGL Tier - II (Quant) (Held On: 8 Aug 2022)
subject: maths
question: The cost price of an article is Rs. 2800. Profit as a percentage of selling price is 20 percent. What is the actual profit (in Rs.) ?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rs. 700**__
**__Key Points__**
__

• According to the question, the **Cost Price (CP)** of the article is **Rs. 2800**.

• The **Profit percentage** is given as **20% of the Selling Price (SP)**. This is different from the usual calculation where profit is a percentage of the Cost Price.

• Let the **Selling Price** be **SP**. We know that **Profit = SP − CP**.

• As per the condition: **Profit = 20% of SP** = (20/100) × SP = **0.2 × SP**.

• Substitute the value of Profit in the basic formula: **0.2 × SP = SP − 2800**.

• Rearrange the equation: **SP − 0.2 × SP = 2800**.

• This simplifies to: **0.8 × SP = 2800**.

• Calculate **SP**: SP = 2800 ÷ 0.8 = **Rs. 3500**.

• Now, the **Actual Profit** = SP − CP = 3500 − 2800 = **Rs. 700**.

• **Alternative Method:** Let SP be 100 units. Then Profit = 20 units. **CP = SP − Profit** = 100 − 20 = 80 units. If 80 units = 2800, then 1 unit = 2800 ÷ 80 = 35. Therefore, Profit (20 units) = 20 × 35 = **Rs. 700**.

**Additional Information__**

• **Profit Margin:** When profit is calculated as a percentage of the **Selling Price**, it is often referred to as the **Profit Margin**.

• **Markup:** When profit is calculated as a percentage of the **Cost Price**, it is known as **Markup**.

• In most standard arithmetic problems, if it is simply mentioned as **Profit Percentage**, it is assumed to be calculated on the **Cost Price** unless specified otherwise.

• Formula for **Profit Percentage on CP**: (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

• Formula for **Profit Percentage on SP**: (Profit ÷ SP) × 100.
